claim: Volatility clusters: a high-vol month tends to be followed by another (AR(1) coefficient of monthly log realised variance 0.6739, 95% CI 0.5816 to 0.7662).
evidence: log_rv_cal / calendar months 1990–2025 / ar1_rho: 0.6739 [0.5816, 0.7662] (Newey–West (6 lags)), HAC z, z = 14.31, p = 1.9e-46
caveat: Persistence fades fast: see the half-life and autocorrelations in the summary.

claim: Volatility shocks fade: realised variance is mean-reverting (augmented Dickey–Fuller statistic -4.803 rejects a unit root).
evidence: log_rv_cal / calendar months 1990–2025 / adf_stat: -4.803, ADF (constant, 4 lags by AIC), H0: unit root, p = 5.4e-05

claim: Realised volatility has risen gradually since 1990 (trend in log realised variance 0.004207 per year, 95% CI -0.01426 to 0.02267).
reasons: calendar months 1990–2025: CI [-0.01426, 0.02267] does not exclude 0
evidence: log_rv_cal / calendar months 1990–2025 / trend_slope_per_year: 0.004207 [-0.01426, 0.02267] (Newey–West (12 lags)), HAC z, z = 0.45, p = 0.66
fallback: Say: there is no evidence of a long-run trend in realised volatility since 1990; it moves in spikes that fade, around a stable level.

claim: Volatility jumps up faster than it falls: month-to-month changes in log realised variance are positively skewed (skewness 0.3437, 95% CI 0.09281 to 0.6042).
evidence: dlog_rv_cal / calendar months 1990–2025 / skewness: 0.3437 [0.09281, 0.6042] (block bootstrap (6-month blocks)), bootstrap, p = 0.008
fallback: Say: month-to-month changes in volatility lean towards sharp rises (positive sample skewness), but the effect does not survive the multiple-testing correction; show it on the chart rather than claim it.

claim: In raw variance the seller earns more when the VIX starts high: VIX > 25 months pay 0.01438 more than VIX ≤ 15 months (95% CI -0.01558 to 0.03655).
reasons: VIX > 25 minus VIX ≤ 15: CI [-0.01558, 0.03655] does not exclude 0
evidence: payoff_var / VIX > 25 minus VIX ≤ 15 / diff_mean_high_minus_low: 0.01438 [-0.01558, 0.03655] (block bootstrap (6-month blocks)), bootstrap, p = 0.27
caveat: Known-at-t buckets, in-sample: a description, not an out-of-sample rule.
fallback: Say: the raw premium is larger on average in VIX > 25 months, but the difference is not significant: high-VIX months also contain the biggest losses.

claim: As a share of implied variance the premium is smaller when the VIX starts high: VIX > 25 minus VIX ≤ 15 = -12.5% (95% CI -41.4% to 11.7%).
reasons: VIX > 25 minus VIX ≤ 15: CI [-0.4142, 0.117] does not exclude 0
evidence: payoff_scaled / VIX > 25 minus VIX ≤ 15 / diff_mean_high_minus_low: -0.1249 [-0.4142, 0.117] (block bootstrap (6-month blocks)), bootstrap, p = 0.35
caveat: Known-at-t buckets, in-sample: a description, not an out-of-sample rule.
fallback: Say: the point estimate is lower in high-VIX months, but we cannot distinguish it from the low-VIX premium.

claim: Even when the VIX starts high (VIX > 25) the seller wins on average: mean scaled payoff 19.0% (95% CI -2.3% to 40.4%).
evidence: payoff_scaled / VIX > 25 / mean: 0.1903 [-0.02323, 0.4037] (Newey–West (6 lags, within bucket)), HAC t, t = 1.75, p = 0.0807
fallback: Say: in VIX > 25 months the seller still wins most months (see the win rate), but the average is not significantly above zero because those months hold the largest crashes.

claim: The premium is larger when the VIX sits well above recent realised vol: gap > 5 pts months pay 19.1% of implied variance more than gap ≤ 0 pts months (95% CI -4.1% to 45.1%).
reasons: gap > 5 pts minus gap ≤ 0 pts: CI [-0.04108, 0.4509] does not exclude 0
evidence: payoff_scaled / gap > 5 pts minus gap ≤ 0 pts / diff_mean_high_minus_low: 0.1907 [-0.04108, 0.4509] (block bootstrap (6-month blocks)), bootstrap, p = 0.13
caveat: Known-at-t buckets, in-sample: a description, not an out-of-sample rule.
fallback: Say: the point estimate is larger when the VIX is well above recent realised vol, but with only a few dozen inverted months the gap is not significant.

claim: The scaled premium has shrunk over time: linear trend -0.8% of implied variance per year (95% CI -1.5% to -0.2%).
evidence: payoff_scaled / monthly 1990–2025 / trend_slope_per_year: -0.008324 [-0.01489, -0.001755] (Newey–West (6 lags)), HAC z, z = -2.48, p = 0.013
caveat: A linear trend through 35 years of spiky data; pre-2003 VIX values are back-calculated. Show the rolling chart next to it.
fallback: Say: there is no significant evidence that the premium is shrinking once we correct for multiple testing.
